narrator: Mina Harker (letter), Lucy Westenra (letter and diary), Dr. John Seward (diary and letters), Arthur Holmwood (letter), Van Helsing (letter); telegrams
summary: Mina reaches Buda-Pesth, finds Jonathan thin and wrecked after brain fever, and marries him at the hospital after he hands her his sealed-away notebook; she wraps it in white paper, ties it with pale blue ribbon and seals it with her wedding ring. Lucy writes cheerfully from Whitby on 30 August, then from Hillingham her sleepwalking and nightmares return, with scratching or flapping at the window, pallor and a sore throat. In London, Seward watches Renfield, who is calm from moonrise to sunrise, escapes twice to the old chapel door of the deserted house (Carfax), and goes quiet when a purposeful big bat flies west. Arthur asks Seward to examine Lucy; Seward finds her blood normal and sends for Van Helsing. Van Helsing examines Lucy, finds no functional cause and goes home to think. Renfield has paroxysms at noon and sunset, drops his fly-collecting abruptly, and says he has been deserted. On 6 September Seward telegraphs Van Helsing that Lucy has suddenly worsened.

scenes.title: Mina finds Jonathan in the hospital
scenes.location: Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth (convent nursing sisters)
scenes.summary: Mina nurses a thin, pale Jonathan. Sister Agatha refuses to repeat his ravings, saying they are secrets of God, but assures Mina his fear was of great and terrible things, not of any wrong he did.
scenes.key_quote: His fear was of great and terrible things, which no mortal can treat of.

scenes.title: The notebook and the wedding
scenes.summary: Jonathan gives Mina the notebook containing his secret and asks her never to tell him unless duty requires. They marry within the hour; Mina wraps the book in white paper, ties it with pale blue ribbon and seals it with her wedding ring.
scenes.key_quote: Take it and keep it, read it if you will, but never let me know

scenes.title: Lucy's cheerful letter
scenes.summary: Lucy reports she has stopped sleepwalking, Arthur is visiting, and the wedding is set for 28 September.
scenes.key_quote: We are to be married on 28 September.

scenes.title: Renfield quiet by moon, violent by day
scenes.summary: Renfield turns calm at moonrise murmuring 'Now I can wait', refuses a kitten, and grows violent again before dawn. Seward decides to give him a chance to escape.
scenes.key_quote: Now I can wait; now I can wait.

scenes.title: Renfield escapes to the chapel door
scenes.location: Grounds of the deserted house (Carfax), old chapel door
scenes.summary: Renfield dashes past an attendant, runs to the old chapel door and presses against it. Held by attendants he redoubles then suddenly calms as a big bat flies silently west across the moon.
scenes.key_quote: a big bat, which was flapping its silent and ghostly way to the west

scenes.title: Lucy's relapse
scenes.summary: Lucy has bad dreams, hears scratching or flapping at the window as the clock strikes twelve, and wakes pale, weak, with a sore throat and air hunger.
scenes.key_quote: There was a sort of scratching or flapping at the window

scenes.title: Arthur's plea and Seward's examination
scenes.summary: Seward lunches at Hillingham, sees Lucy drop her cheerful mask in the boudoir, accidentally obtains a few drops of her blood from a broken window-cord cut, finds it normal, and writes to Van Helsing.
scenes.key_quote: The qualitative analysis gives a quite normal condition

scenes.title: Van Helsing examines Lucy
scenes.summary: Van Helsing charms Lucy, sends Seward to smoke in the garden, examines her privately, notes blood loss but no anaemia, asks to question her maid, and goes home to think while demanding daily telegrams.
scenes.key_quote: This is no jest, but life and death, perhaps more.

scenes.title: Renfield's noon and sunset fits
scenes.summary: Renfield is violent at noon, then collects flies with sugar on the window sill, then at sunset collapses as the sun dips, throws away his fly-box and declares he is done with flies, saying 'He has deserted me'.
scenes.key_quote: All over! all over! He has deserted me.

scenes.title: Telegrams: Lucy worsens
scenes.summary: Two reassuring telegrams are followed by an urgent call on 6 September.
scenes.key_quote: Terrible change for the worse. Come at once; do not lose an hour.

locations.name: Hospital of St. Joseph and Ste. Mary, Buda-Pesth
locations.description: A convent hospital run by sisters, with a Superior and a chaplain of the English mission church. Jonathan lies propped on pillows in a bed by a window.
locations.quote: I am now sitting by his bedside, where I can see his face while he sleeps.

locations.name: Renfield's padded room
locations.description: Padded cell in Seward's asylum; the door edge between ridges of padding bears Renfield's nail-mark tally of caught flies.
locations.quote: making nail-marks on the edge of the door between the ridges of padding

locations.name: Renfield's own room
locations.description: A normal asylum room with a window that opens; sugar spread on the sill attracts flies, kept in a box.
locations.quote: He has the sugar of his tea spread out on the window-sill

locations.name: Grounds of the deserted house and old chapel door
locations.description: Overgrown grounds next to the asylum; the old chapel door is where Renfield presses himself.
locations.quote: pressed against the old chapel door

locations.name: Seward's asylum exterior and gate
locations.description: Cold stone building seen at a gate with a smoky London sunset behind it.
locations.atmosphere: grim contrast of lurid sunset and desolate institution
locations.quote: all the grim sternness of my own cold stone building, with its wealth of breathing misery

locations.name: Hillingham, Lucy's bedroom
locations.description: Lucy's room with a window where scratching/flapping is heard; a clock strikes twelve.
locations.quote: when the clock struck twelve it waked me from a doze

locations.name: Hillingham boudoir
locations.description: Lucy's private sitting room with a stiff window whose cord breaks.

characters.personality: fragile, honest, fears he was mad
characters.speech_style: formal, calls her Wilhelmina in earnest
notable_lines: I do not know if it was all real or the dreaming of a madman.

characters.name: Sister Agatha
notable_lines: the ravings of the sick were the secrets of God

characters.name: Lucy Westenra
characters.personality: sweet, brave, hides her illness for others
notable_lines: Tell Arthur everything you choose. I do not care for myself, but all for him!

characters.name: Dr. John Seward
notable_lines: Happy thought! We shall to-night play sane wits against mad ones.

characters.name: Renfield
notable_lines: They think I could hurt you! Fancy me hurting you! The fools!
I don't take any stock in cats.

characters.name: Abraham Van Helsing
notable_lines: There is always cause for everything.

objects.quote: I took the book from under his pillow, and wrapped it up in white paper, and tied it with a little bit of pale blue ribbon

creatures.name: Big bat
creatures.description: Large bat that flies silently and straight, not wheeling like ordinary bats, heading west from the moonlit sky.
creatures.behaviour: Purposeful; calms Renfield when seen; scratches or flaps at Lucy's window (implied).
creatures.quote: as if it knew where it was bound for or had some intention of its own

creatures.name: Flies and spiders
creatures.description: Renfield's collected insects; he looks for a spider.
creatures.quote: is already examining the corners of his room to find a spider

vampire_lore.rule: Renfield's moods follow moonrise/sunrise and noon/sunset
vampire_lore.detail: Calm from moonrise to sunrise, violent by day; later paroxysms at high noon and at sunset, suggesting a link to the Count's presence or waking.
vampire_lore.quote: Three nights has the same thing happened—violent all day then quiet from moonrise to sunrise.

vampire_lore.rule: Vampire can appear as a bat and act purposefully
vampire_lore.detail: A bat flying straight west controls Renfield's calm.
vampire_lore.quote: a big bat, which was flapping its silent and ghostly way to the west

vampire_lore.rule: Victim suffers sleepwalking, pallor, weakness and neck pain while normal tests find nothing
vampire_lore.detail: Lucy's blood is normal but she is bloodless in appearance.
vampire_lore.quote: My face is ghastly pale, and my throat pains me.

vampire_lore.rule: Scratching or flapping at the window at midnight precedes bad nights
vampire_lore.quote: There was a sort of scratching or flapping at the window

puzzles.name: Why does Renfield rest only at night?
puzzles.setup: Renfield alternates between violence and calm in a daily pattern.
puzzles.obstacle: Find the cause of his moods.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward notes the pattern, lets him escape under watch, and links paroxysms to noon and sunset.
puzzles.game_idea: Timeline puzzle: log Renfield's behaviour over several in-game days to deduce the timing pattern and predict his next episode.
puzzles.quote: Can it be that there is a malign influence of the sun at periods

puzzles.name: Diagnose Lucy
puzzles.setup: Lucy is pale and weak with no disease.
puzzles.obstacle: Rule out anaemia and find the cause.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward tests the blood from a cut; Van Helsing examines her and concludes blood has been lost but she is not anaemic.
puzzles.game_idea: Clue-collecting diagnosis mini-game: examine symptoms, run blood test, question the maid, choose a hypothesis.
puzzles.quote: there has been much blood lost; it has been, but is not.

combat.name: Restraining Renfield
combat.tactics: Several attendants hold him; he redoubles strength then drops calm when the bat appears.
combat.outcome: Held and returned to the asylum.
combat.game_idea: Non-lethal restraint encounter: reduce his agitation meter by timing grabs while a hidden trigger (the bat) can swing it.
combat.quote: it took all their strength to hold him

crafting.method: Wrap in white paper, tie ribbon, melt wax over knot, press ring.
